clue.text: Where Beach Boys have been seen arranging one album

definitions.text: Where Beach Boys have been seen

indicators.note: arranging puts the letters of the following words into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A pop band photographed on the shore while putting together a record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranging' shuffles I (one) with ALBUM. The Beach Boys are the Californian surf band, not just any lads on the sand.
explanation.definitionFit: This Californian coastal resort is famous surfing territory, just where the surf-rock group would be pictured.

clue.text: June 1926, US film star

parts.note: the clue number 1 supplies the day, so this is an American screen actress born on the first of June 1926

explanation.walkthrough: In this puzzle the bare clues are birthdays: the clue's number is the day of the month, so 1-down is someone born on 1 June 1926.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hollywood icon born Norma Jeane Mortenson came into the world on 1 June 1926 in Los Angeles.

clue.text: Learner badly upset by stoppages

parts.note: L is the learner driver's plate abbreviation

indicators.note: badly says the letters of the next word are messed up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A driving student is thrown into distress by repeated hold-ups on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the anagram fodder's mood, and 'badly' its degree; the hyphenated plural is the everyday word for pauses.
explanation.definitionFit: Pauses or slackenings in activity are interruptions, so the hyphenated plural means halts.

clue.text: August 1926, US singer

parts.note: the clue number 3 supplies the day, so this is an American vocalist born on the third of August 1926

explanation.walkthrough: The clue number is the birthday: 3 August 1926.
explanation.definitionFit: The crooner of I Left My Heart in San Francisco was born in Queens on 3 August 1926.

clue.text: Some Charlie covering up an appalling mess one's seen on board

indicators.note: covering up says the detective's surname wraps around and conceals the next piece

parts.note: Charlie Chan is a famous fictional detective, one particular Charlie

indicators.note: appalling signals that the letters of the following word are turned into a horrible jumble

explanation.surface: Someone using cocaine hides a dreadful mess they have made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some Charlie' is one particular Charlie, the fictional detective Charlie Chan; 'an' is only a link. 'appalling' scrambles MESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece used in a board game such as a knight or bishop is something seen on the chequered board.

clue.text: Old actor at start of highlights is accompanied by band

indicators.note: at start of points to the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written
a trio is a band of three musicians

explanation.surface: A veteran performer begins his highlights reel backed by a group of musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at start of' takes H from 'highlights'; 'accompanied by' simply joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for a stage player, used in English for an actor of the ancient or old-fashioned sort.

clue.text: Roman dramatist rewriting scene one

indicators.note: rewriting means the given letters are reworked into a fresh order

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A classical playwright revising a single scene of his drama.
explanation.walkthrough: Seneca the Younger, Nero's tutor, wrote the tragedies; 'one' is the article A, set after the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Stoic philosopher wrote tragedies such as Phaedra and Thyestes in imperial Rome.

clue.text: August 1876, World War I spy

parts.note: the clue number 7 supplies the day, so this is an espionage figure of the Great War born on the seventh of August 1876

explanation.walkthrough: The clue number gives the day: 7 August 1876.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch exotic dancer Margaretha Zelle, executed by France in 1917 for espionage, was born on 7 August 1876.

clue.text: "Stand not amazed. Here is " (Merry Wives of Windsor)

definitions.text: "Stand not amazed. Here is " (Merry Wives of Windsor)

parts.words: "Stand not amazed. Here is " (Merry Wives of Windsor)
parts.note: a quotation with its last words missing: in the final scene Ford tells the company that nothing can now be done about the marriage

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: Ford goes on, 'In love the heavens themselves do guide the state'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing two words complete Ford's line accepting Fenton's elopement with Anne Page as beyond any cure.

clue.text: April 1926, US magazine publisher

parts.note: the clue number 9 supplies the day, so this is an American periodical owner born on the ninth of April 1926

explanation.walkthrough: The clue number gives the day: 9 April 1926.
explanation.definitionFit: The founder of Playboy magazine was born in Chicago on 9 April 1926.

clue.text: I must abandon confused Tina Turner in revolt

indicators.note: confused says the letters of the singer's first name are scrambled
must abandon says the letter named first has to leave the jumbled pool

explanation.surface: Advice to someone muddled about the singer Tina Turner rebelling.
explanation.walkthrough: Take I out of TINA and rearrange what is left. 'Turner' looks like the singer's surname; it is the slave who led the 1831 Virginia uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: The enslaved preacher who led the 1831 rebellion in Southampton County, Virginia is known by this short first name.

clue.text: February 1926, US film actor

parts.note: the clue number 11 supplies the day, so this is a screen actor working in America born on the eleventh of February 1926

explanation.walkthrough: The clue number gives the day: 11 February 1926.
explanation.definitionFit: The deadpan star of Airplane! and The Naked Gun was born in Regina, Saskatchewan, on 11 February 1926.

clue.text: Hill that's no height for a Norse God

indicators.note: that's no means the name is left without the letter for the following word

parts.note: Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: A mountain too low to suit a deity of Scandinavian myth.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes first; 'that's no' removes H from THOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A craggy rocky peak, especially on Dartmoor in south-west England, is called this.

clue.text: Melodious harp one's playing

indicators.note: playing is the anagram signal: the letters are played about with

parts.note: the possessive is no letter, giving just one

explanation.surface: A musician is plucking a sweet-sounding harp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges HARP with ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after the mythical Greek musician whose lyre charmed beasts, so the adjective means tuneful.

clue.text: Illustrator to stress poor actor

parts.note: to rack is to strain or put under stress
a ham is a bad, overacting performer

explanation.surface: An artist is told to put pressure on an incompetent performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Rackham was the English illustrator of fairy tales and Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edwardian artist known for his spidery, twisted-tree pictures for children's books was a famous illustrator.

clue.text: Dickensian friend's beginning to work

parts.note: a start is a beginning
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Something from Dickens about the first steps in a job.
explanation.walkthrough: Startop is Pip's fellow pupil and rowing companion in Great Expectations; 'friend's' is 'friend is'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Great Expectations this young gentleman befriends Pip at Mr Pocket's house and helps with Magwitch's escape.

clue.text: Japanese writer, one with an engineering degree

parts.note: one is A, the indefinite article
BE is Bachelor of Engineering

explanation.surface: A novelist from Japan who happens to have trained as an engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: Kobo Abe wrote The Woman in the Dunes.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of The Woman in the Dunes was a Japanese novelist, and he really had studied medicine, not engineering.

clue.text: Round up Joey perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a lap is one round of a track

explanation.surface: An instruction to collect a young kangaroo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joey' suggests a baby kangaroo, but the reference is the musical Pal Joey.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of the Rodgers and Hart musical Pal Joey makes its hero an example of a mate.

clue.text: Loud colourful member of the Flintstone family

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
red is a strong colour

explanation.surface: A noisy, brightly dressed character from the Stone Age cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: The cartoon caveman father in Bedrock, husband of Wilma, heads the Flintstone household.

clue.text: February 1876, Romanian sculptor and painter

parts.note: the clue number 19 supplies the day, so this is an artist from Romania born on the nineteenth of February 1876

explanation.walkthrough: The clue number gives the day: 19 February 1876.
explanation.definitionFit: Constantin, the modernist who made Bird in Space and The Kiss, was born in Hobița, Romania, on 19 February 1876.

clue.text: Erskine in Scotland sounds like a source of icy water

indicators.note: the phrase says the words are spoken in a Scottish accent, where cold is pronounced cauld

parts.note: a cold well, which in Scots is a cauld well

explanation.surface: A man called Erskine, living north of the border, is said to be like a chilly spring.
explanation.walkthrough: Erskine Caldwell was the American novelist of Tobacco Road. 'Erskine' also hints at Scottish names, but it is the first name of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of Tobacco Road and God's Little Acre bore the first name Erskine.

clue.text: Sincere production of Lear

indicators.note: a production of a play reworks it, so the letters of the title are rearranged

explanation.surface: A heartfelt staging of Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'production of' rearranges LEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Genuine feelings are authentic, not pretended, so the word means heartfelt.

clue.text: Food that's tender, rejected by English and the French

indicators.note: rejected says the word is turned back the other way

parts.note: to tender is to offer, as in a bid
les is the French plural for the

explanation.surface: Something to eat that is soft enough, yet both the English and French turn it down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' looks like a description of meat, but it means an offer; 'rejected' reverses BID to DIB.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that are fit to eat are often called this, as a plural noun for foodstuffs.

clue.text: November 1876, Spanish composer (?)

parts.note: the clue number 23 supplies the day, so this is a composer from Spain born on the twenty-third of November 1876

explanation.walkthrough: The clue number gives the day: 23 November 1876. The question mark flags that the entry includes the particle of the surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Manuel, the Andalusian composer of The Three-Cornered Hat and Nights in the Gardens of Spain, was born in Cádiz on 23 November 1876.

clue.text: May 1926, Scottish comedian

parts.note: the clue number 24 supplies the day, so this is a comic performer from Scotland born on the twenty-fourth of May 1926

explanation.walkthrough: The clue number gives the day: 24 May 1926.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley, the Glasgow-born actor and television comic famed for impersonations and pantomime, was born on 24 May 1926.

clue.text: Time to get you French on board with a Greek official

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: on, as in on board, means put aboard, inside the ship's letters

parts.note: board here is the ship you go on board, the steamship, SS
tu is the familiar French for you

explanation.surface: Instructions for a moment when a Frenchman joins a Hellenic dignitary aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: Erastus is the treasurer of Corinth sent greetings in Paul's letter to the Romans.
explanation.definitionFit: In the New Testament this man was chamberlain or treasurer of the city of Corinth, a civic officer in Greece.

clue.text: Dawkins primarily a chap not getting caught

definitions.meaning: Jack Dawkins in Oliver Twist is known chiefly by his nickname, the Artful one
someone who evades capture, slipping out of trouble

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dawkins' suggests the biologist Richard, but it is Jack Dawkins, the pickpocket in Dickens's Oliver Twist, called mainly by his nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: The pickpocket Jack Dawkins goes chiefly by his nickname, and anyone who evades capture is also this.

clue.text: John Williams's teacher has a way with one basic element of education

parts.note: St, street, is a way
taken as written
the three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic, so R is one of them

explanation.surface: A guitar maestro's tutor finds a route to the fundamentals of schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: John Williams suggests the guitarist or film composer; it is the American novelist whose Stoner is about a university teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: William Stoner, title character of John Williams's 1965 novel, spends his life as an English professor at Missouri.

clue.text: June 1926, US actor-director

parts.note: the clue number 28 supplies the day, so this is an American performer and film-maker born on the twenty-eighth of June 1926

explanation.walkthrough: The clue number gives the day: 28 June 1926.
explanation.definitionFit: Mel, maker of The Producers and Blazing Saddles, was born in Brooklyn on 28 June 1926.

clue.text: Goes to sleep with lecturer coming over so very loud

indicators.note: coming over means the word turns over, read right to left

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer
taken as written
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: Someone dozes off while a noisy lecturer visits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming over' reverses DON to NOD.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means drops off into a doze, as a tired person's head droops.

clue.text: Screen category for including variety turn in a talent show

parts.note: X was the old British film certificate for adults only

indicators.note: including says the first word wraps around the following piece

parts.note: an act is a turn on a variety bill

explanation.surface: Which film rating suits a music-hall routine on a TV talent contest.
explanation.walkthrough: The X certificate was the old adults-only cinema rating in Britain; The X Factor is a British TV talent contest.
explanation.definitionFit: The televised singing contest judged by Simon Cowell is a talent competition broadcast in Britain.

clue.text: Country and electronic music played on this?

parts.note: UK is the abbreviation for United Kingdom
E is short for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: An instrument for playing country and electronic music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' and 'electronic' look like genres of music, but give UK and E.
explanation.definitionFit: The ukulele, a small four-stringed instrument, is what music would be strummed on.

clue.text: Bronte narrator mark im we're told

definitions.text: Bronte narrator mark im we're told

parts.words: Bronte narrator mark im we're told
parts.note: the narrator of Anne Bronte's The Tenant of Wildfell Hall is surnamed Markham, which said aloud is 'mark him'; the entry is his first name

explanation.walkthrough: The narrator of The Tenant of Wildfell Hall is Gilbert Markham; 'mark im', said aloud, gives the surname, and the entry is his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Bronte's novel is told in letters by the young farmer who loves Helen Graham, and that is his Christian name.

clue.text: Language spoken by one in The Matrix?

definitions.meaning: an invented international language of the 1930s bore this name
the hero of the Matrix films, played by Keanu Reeves, who is called The One

explanation.walkthrough: 'one' hints at the film's chosen hero, called The One.
explanation.definitionFit: Keanu Reeves's hacker hero in The Matrix bears this name, which is also that of a constructed auxiliary language.

clue.text: Troublesome time in short, meeting a chap like Orsino

parts.note: ill can mean bad or troublesome, as in ill omens
yr is the short form of year
Ian is a man's name, any chap

explanation.surface: A difficult spell, when a man resembling Shakespeare's lovesick duke shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: Orsino is the Duke of Illyria in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night.
explanation.definitionFit: In Twelfth Night the duke rules a land on the Adriatic, so he is a native of that coast.

clue.text: Apocryphal character recklessly dares to swear at first

indicators.note: recklessly signals the letters of the preceding word are thrown about wildly
at first means only the opening letter of the word before is taken

explanation.surface: A figure from legend boldly challenges people to curse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recklessly' rearranges DARES into ESDRA; 'at first' gives S from 'swear'. The Apocrypha are the books outside the Hebrew Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: The books named after the scribe Ezra in the Apocrypha carry this Greek form of his name.
